_about: Isobutanol (1) + Tetrahydrofuran (2): isobaric bubble temperatures at 95.8 kPa (no vapour compositions are fitted). Rows: liquid mole fraction of isobutanol, boiling temperature in K, as stored in the ThermoML Archive record (mole fractions of the other component converted with x_1 = 1 - x_2).

source.citation: T. E. V. Prasad, E. D. A. Raj, G. Maheedhar, M. S. Reddy, V. Kumar, S. Garapati, V. Patanjali, D. H. L. Prasad, Bubble-Temperature Measurements on Some Binary Mixtures Formed by Tetrahydrofuran or Amyl Alcohol with Hydrocarbons, Chlorohydrocarbons, or Butanols at (94.6 or 95.8) kPa, J. Chem. Eng. Data 49 (2004) 746-749
source.access: The journal article may be subscription-only; the same data is public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (NIST open license).
source.tables: ThermoML record, PureOrMixtureData 52. The table number in the article was not checked.

notes: Read with validation/python/vle_batch.py. Fitted to the bubble temperatures alone (Barker's method): no set of this pair with vapour compositions passes the consistency point test, or none was measured. Pure-component boiling points of the set within 0.38 K of the vapour-pressure records. To be checked by a person against the record (AGENTS.md rule 4).
